content: The recommended dosing for P57, also known as Hoodia, is 250-750 mg taken orally two to four times daily as an appetite suppressant. Traditionally, Hoodia has been used by the San Bushmen of South Africa to suppress appetite. P57 is a steroidal glycoside that is believed to have pharmacological activity and has been isolated for clinical trials. In one study, large doses of P57 were shown to reduce daily caloric intake by approximately 100 calories by Day 15 in a small group of healthy but overweight individuals. Although many weight loss supplements claim to contain Hoodia, the actual amount and efficacy of the ingredient in these products remain unverified. No adverse effects have been reported in clinical studies, but it is known to suppress thirst in addition to appetite. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific categorization or data available for P57. However, it is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated evidence of fetal risk.
